day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use the Aerobus or Metro (Line 1 - Red Line) from Lisbon Airport to the city center for around €1.80–€3.00. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a relaxed walk through the historic Baixa (Downtown) district. Stroll along Rua Augusta, pass through the iconic Arco da Rua Augusta (exterior is free to admire), and head down to Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River. Soak in the views of the river and the grand yellow square — completely free and quintessentially Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Bairro Alto or Mouraria neighborhood for your first taste of authentic Lisbon nightlife and local food culture. Explore the narrow streets and enjoy the relaxed atmosphere. Pop into a local tasca (traditional tavern) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastel de nata (custard tart, ~€1.20) and a bica (espresso, ~€0.80) at a local café near the airport or hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a light bifana (pork sandwich, ~€2–€3) from a street kiosk or bakery in Baixa while exploring.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local tasca in Mouraria or Alfama — look for the 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) which typically costs €7–€10 and includes soup, main, and sometimes a drink. Try bacalhau à brás (shredded cod with eggs and potatoes).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a rechargeable Viva Viagem card at the airport metro station (~€0.50 card fee) and load it with credit for cheap metro, tram, and bus rides throughout the trip. Validate your transport card every time you board.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to the Alfama district, Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood. Climb up to the Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro de Santa Luzia for panoramic views over the city and the Tagus — both are free. Then visit the exterior and surrounding streets of the São Jorge Castle (entry ~€15, or admire from outside to save budget).
day_by_day.afternoon: Make your way to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience in the Cais do Sodré area. Spend 2–3 hours grazing through Lisbon's iconic food hall featuring the best local chefs and traditional dishes. Sample small portions from multiple stalls — budget around €15–€20 for a satisfying self-guided tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Alfama area to experience authentic Fado music. Many small restaurants and tascas in Alfama offer free Fado performances in the evening while you dine. Arrive early (around 7:30 PM) to secure a table.

meals.breakfast: Start at a local padaria (bakery) near the hotel — coffee and a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) for under €3.
meals.lunch: Lunch IS the Time Out Market experience — graze on petiscos (Portuguese tapas), fresh seafood, and traditional bites. Budget €15–€20.
meals.dinner: Dine at a Fado house tasca in Alfama. Look for set menus around €12–€15 that include a main course and house wine, with live Fado included.

day_by_day.notes: Alfama's cobblestone streets are steep and uneven — wear comfortable walking shoes. Saturday mornings are lively in Alfama with local markets. The Feira da Ladra flea market is nearby at Campo de Santa Clara if you want to browse (free entry).

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or bus out to Belém (about 20–30 minutes from the city center, ~€1.80 each way on the Viva Viagem card). Begin your Belém Historical Monuments visit with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery — a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture. Entry to the main church is FREE; the cloister costs ~€10 (or free on Sunday mornings until 2 PM for EU citizens — check current policy).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém with a visit to the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém), another UNESCO World Heritage site and symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery. Entry is ~€6. Afterward, walk along the riverfront promenade and visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) — exterior viewing is free. Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) for the authentic pastel de nata experience (~€1.30 each).
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the city center and explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood, known for its charming garden, antique shops, and local restaurants. Browse the Sunday antiques market in Jardim do Príncipe Real (free). Settle in for a relaxed Sunday dinner at a neighborhood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast near the hotel before heading out — coffee and pastry at a local café, ~€2–€3.
meals.lunch: Eat near Belém — try a simple restaurant along Rua de Belém offering prato do dia for €8–€10, or pick up fresh bread, cheese, and presunto (cured ham) from a local shop for a riverside picnic (~€5–€7).
meals.dinner: Dine in Príncipe Real at a local tasca. Try grilled sardines (sardinhas grelhadas) or caldo verde (kale soup) with a main for under €12–€15 total.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is best explored on foot once you arrive. The waterfront walk between the Monastery and the Tower of Belém is scenic and pleasant. Sunday can be busy — arrive at Jerónimos Monastery by 9:30 AM to beat the crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — a fascinating journey through five centuries of Portugal's iconic azulejo tile art. Entry is €5 (reduced) or €10 standard; free on the first Sunday of the month. Allow 2–3 hours to explore the stunning collection housed in a former convent, including a magnificent 23-meter panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, make your way to the Mouraria neighborhood — the historic Moorish quarter and birthplace of Fado. Explore the colorful streets, street art, and the lively Intendente square. Visit the free Museu do Fado (check for free entry days) to learn about the history of this soulful music genre. Browse the local market stalls and interact with residents.
day_by_day.evening: Climb up to the Miradouro da Senhora do Monte — Lisbon's highest viewpoint — for a spectacular panoramic sunset view over the entire city. It's completely free and less touristy than other miradouros. Afterward, have dinner in the Graça neighborhood, which is very local and affordable.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a croissant or pastel de nata at a café near the hotel, ~€2–€3.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant near the Tile Museum or in Mouraria — prato do dia for €8–€10. Try arroz de pato (duck rice) if available.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Graça neighborhood — find a simple local tasca offering hearty Portuguese comfort food. Try prego no pão (steak sandwich) or a full meal for under €10–€12.

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is a short bus or Uber ride from the city center (Bus 718 or 742). Monday can be a quiet day at museums — a good time to visit without large crowds. Check the museum's website for any temporary exhibitions.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your last morning exploring the Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods — Lisbon's cultural and bohemian heart. Visit the beautiful Igreja do Carmo (Carmo Convent) ruins, a hauntingly beautiful Gothic church destroyed in the 1755 earthquake — entry ~€5. Browse the charming bookshops, including the historic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop, free to enter). Ride the iconic Elevador da Glória or Elevador da Bica funiculars (~€3.90 round trip) for a fun and scenic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Mercado de Campo de Ourique, a more local and less touristy food market than Time Out, for a final afternoon of Portuguese food exploration. Sample petiscos, local cheeses, charcuterie, and wines at very reasonable prices. Then take a final stroll along the Tagus riverfront at Cais do Sodré and Ribeira to enjoy the city one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell dinner in the Bairro Alto or Cais do Sodré area. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate the trip — a full traditional Portuguese dinner with wine should still come in under €20 per person at a good local restaurant. End the night with a ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur, ~€1.50) at one of the tiny historic ginjinha bars in Rossio square.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a local pastelaria — galão (milky coffee), pastel de nata, and a torrada (toast with butter) for ~€4.
meals.lunch: Graze at Mercado de Campo de Ourique — pick and mix petiscos, cheese, and a glass of wine for €10–€15.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional restaurant in Bairro Alto — try bacalhau com natas (creamy cod gratin) or a mixed seafood cataplana. Budget €15–€20 including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is the next day, pack your bags the night before and confirm transport to the airport. The Aerobus or Metro Red Line are the most budget-friendly options (~€1.80–€3.60). Keep some coins handy for the ginjinha bars in Rossio — they only serve in tiny shot glasses and it's a quintessential Lisbon experience.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line) to central Lisbon (~30–40 min, budget-friendly). Check in to Lisbon City Stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed self-guided stroll through the Baixa-Chiado neighborhood — explore Praça do Comércio, the waterfront Tagus promenade, and the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa for a first taste of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon (Mercado da Ribeira) for your first real Lisbon meal. Graze through stalls from award-winning local chefs — try a bifana (pork sandwich), fresh seafood, and a glass of Vinho Verde. Lively, authentic, and perfect for jet-lagged first-night energy.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick pastel de nata and coffee at a café near the airport arrivals hall (e.g., Café Flor do Aeroporto) — under €5.
meals.lunch: Light snack on arrival — grab a tostas mistas (toasted ham & cheese sandwich) at a Baixa café near the hotel for €3–5.
meals.dinner: Time Out Market Lisbon — budget €15–25 per person for a satisfying multi-dish grazing experience with a drink included.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally relaxed given the 13:00 arrival. Prioritize orientation and a gentle introduction to the city. Pick up a Lisboa Card at the airport or a metro station for multi-day transport savings. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance in case the room isn't ready until 15:00.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a proper Portuguese breakfast at a local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee (bica) and pastéis de nata for under €5. Then head to the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) when it opens at 10:00. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring five centuries of Portugal's iconic azulejo tile art, including a stunning panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tram or walk to the Mouraria Neighborhood Food & History Walk. Wander Lisbon's ancient Moorish quarter at your own pace — discover hidden squares, street art, the Intendente neighborhood, and stop at local tabernas for petiscos (Portuguese tapas). Visit the Mouraria market stalls if open on Sunday.
day_by_day.evening: Book the Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show for the evening. Explore the medieval alleyways of Lisbon's oldest neighborhood with a guide, visit miradouros (viewpoints) at dusk, and cap the night with a live Fado performance — Portugal's soulful, UNESCO-recognized music tradition.

meals.breakfast: Local pastelaria near hotel — bica + pastel de nata, €3–5.
meals.lunch: Petiscos lunch in Mouraria — try A Cevicheria or a neighborhood tasca for grilled sardines, chouriço, and bread. Budget €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner included or paired with the Fado show experience in Alfama — typically a set dinner with wine. Budget €30–45 per person depending on the venue chosen.

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays, so visiting on Sunday is ideal. Book the Fado show in advance as weekend performances sell out quickly. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Alfama and Mouraria have steep cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train from Cais do Sodré station to Belém (15 min, ~€1.50 each way). Arrive early to beat the crowds at the iconic Jerónimos Monastery — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and masterpiece of Manueline architecture. Spend 1–1.5 hours exploring the elaborate cloisters and the tomb of Vasco da Gama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Tagus riverfront to the Tower of Belém — another UNESCO landmark and symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery. Afterward, visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) for panoramic views. Then make the essential pilgrimage to Pastéis de Belém — the original custard tart bakery since 1837 — for a fresh tart dusted with cinnamon and powdered sugar.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood — a charming, upscale-bohemian district with antique shops, wine bars, and garden squares. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a croissant at a café near Cais do Sodré before boarding the train — €4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Belém — try Solar dos Presuntos or a riverside café for grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia), salad, and wine. Budget €15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Príncipe Real — try Taberna da Rua das Flores or a similar mid-range tasca for traditional Portuguese dishes like bacalhau à brás (salt cod) or carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams). Budget €20–30 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays for the main church but the cloisters may still be accessible — verify hours before visiting. Arrive at Pastéis de Belém before or after the main lunch rush to avoid long queues. The Belém area is flat and very walkable along the river.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour experience — arrive when the market opens and take a structured or self-guided deep dive into Lisbon's best culinary offerings. Sample dishes from top local chefs including fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and regional specialties. Pair with a glass of local wine or ginjinha (cherry liqueur).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, walk or take a tram to the Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods. Browse independent bookshops (including the famous Livraria Bertrand, the world's oldest operating bookshop), explore art galleries, and visit the Igreja do Carmo — a hauntingly beautiful Gothic church ruined by the 1755 earthquake and left open to the sky as a museum.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bairro Alto's vibrant bar scene for pre-dinner drinks — try a craft beer at a local cervejaria or a glass of port wine. Dinner at a traditional restaurant in Chiado or Bairro Alto, then a leisurely evening walk along the Tagus waterfront at Cais do Sodré.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — toast, juice, and coffee, €4–7.
meals.lunch: The Time Out Market food tour IS the main midday meal — budget €20–30 per person for a satisfying multi-dish grazing experience across several vendors.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Chiado — try Tasca do Chico or Cervejaria Ramiro (for seafood) — budget €22–35 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Time Out Market is busiest on weekends; a Tuesday visit means shorter queues and a more local crowd. Igreja do Carmo charges a small entry fee (~€5) and is well worth it for history lovers. Bairro Alto restaurants typically open for dinner from 19:30 onward.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, leisurely final morning — sleep in or take an early walk to Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro da Senhora do Monte for the best panoramic views over Lisbon's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. Enjoy a long, relaxed café breakfast in the Graça neighborhood — one of Lisbon's most authentic and least touristy districts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use the afternoon for any missed sights, souvenir shopping (Rua Augusta in Baixa for azulejo tiles, cork goods, and local wine), or a visit to the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Ancient Art Museum) if time permits. Alternatively, take a scenic Tram 28 ride through the historic hills of Lisbon for a final cinematic tour of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special mid-range restaurant — consider a rooftop terrace restaurant in Alfama or Mouraria for views and atmosphere. Toast to the trip with a glass of Moscatel de Setúbal dessert wine and a final pastel de nata before heading back to the hotel to pack.

meals.breakfast: Long café breakfast in Graça neighborhood — fresh orange juice, eggs, toast, and bica. Budget €7–10 per person.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Baixa during shopping — try a traditional soup (caldo verde) and a prego (steak sandwich) at a local tasca. Budget €8–14 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range restaurant with views — budget €28–40 per person with wine. Try Chapitô à Mesa or Páteo de Alfama for atmosphere and quality.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is later in the day. Tram 28 can be very crowded — consider going early afternoon or using it as a one-way scenic ride rather than a full loop. Leave time to buy last-minute gifts: local wine, tinned fish (conservas), and ceramic tiles make excellent mid-range souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Lisbon City Stay via private luxury transfer. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the nearby Chiado and Baixa districts to orient yourself with the city. Browse the elegant boutiques on Rua Garrett and admire the iconic Santa Justa Lift. Stop at the Miradouro de Santa Catarina for sweeping panoramic views over the Tagus River — a perfect gentle introduction to Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show: Begin the evening with a guided walk through Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood, winding through medieval alleyways, past the São Jorge Castle walls and colorful tiled facades. Cap the night with an authentic Fado performance at a traditional casa de fado, where Portugal's soul-stirring music fills the candlelit room.

meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at Guilty by Olivier (Chiado) — a stylish Portuguese bistro serving elevated local classics. Try the bacalhau à brás and a glass of Vinho Verde upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Fado show experience, or dine beforehand at Zé da Mouraria, a beloved neighborhood restaurant serving traditional Lisbon cuisine with rustic charm and exceptional quality.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm the Fado show reservation prior to travel as top houses book out quickly. Pack comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets of Alfama.

day_by_day.morning: National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo): Begin the day with a visit to one of Lisbon's most unique and visually stunning museums. Explore five centuries of Portuguese azulejo tile artistry housed in a gorgeous 16th-century convent. Highlights include the extraordinary 36-meter panoramic tile panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon and the ornate Baroque chapel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mouraria Neighborhood Food & History Walk: Head to Lisbon's oldest Moorish quarter for a small-group culinary and history experience. Discover hidden tabernas, local market stalls, and historic mosques-turned-churches while sampling traditional petiscos (Portuguese tapas), ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur), and artisan cheeses from local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset aperitivo at a rooftop bar such as TOPO Chiado or Park Bar, with sweeping views over Lisbon's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. Follow with an indulgent dinner at a premier Lisbon restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. If not included, visit Nicolau Lisboa in Chiado for exceptional pastries, avocado toast, and specialty coffee in a beautifully designed space.
meals.lunch: Petiscos and local tastings during the Mouraria Food Walk — included as part of the experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alma (1 Michelin Star) — Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's flagship restaurant offering a refined modern Portuguese tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings. Advance reservation essential.

day_by_day.notes: The Tile Museum is best visited early to avoid weekend crowds. Mouraria is most vibrant mid-afternoon when local vendors and residents fill the squares. Book Alma restaurant well in advance — it is one of Lisbon's most sought-after tables.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastéis de Belém: Take a private or chauffeured transfer to the historic Belém district along the Tagus riverfront. Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture built to honor Vasco da Gama's voyage to India. Explore the soaring cloisters and ornate church at a leisurely, unhurried pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the iconic Tower of Belém, Portugal's most photographed monument, standing sentinel at the river's edge. Visit the nearby Monument to the Discoveries and stroll the riverside promenade. Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery for the original, warm-from-the-oven custard tarts (pastel de nata) — a non-negotiable Lisbon ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the elegant Príncipe Real neighborhood, known for its antique shops, designer boutiques, and sophisticated garden square. Enjoy a relaxed, refined evening with cocktails and dinner in this upscale residential quarter.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pastéis de nata and espresso at a local café in Belém before the monastery opens.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solar dos Presuntos (if returning to Chiado) or at Belém's Estufa Real restaurant, set within a stunning 19th-century greenhouse in the Ajuda Botanical Garden — an extraordinary and atmospheric dining setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Cevicheria or Taberna da Rua das Flores in Chiado — both celebrated for creative, ingredient-driven Portuguese cuisine in intimate, design-forward settings.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery can have queues on Sunday mornings; arriving at opening time (10:00) is strongly recommended. Book a private guide for a richer historical narrative of the Manueline architectural details. Belém is approximately 6–7 km west of central Lisbon — a scenic riverside taxi or Uber ride.

day_by_day.morning: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Spend a curated morning at Lisbon's iconic food hall in the Cais do Sodré district. Work with a local food guide (or explore independently) to graze through stalls helmed by the city's best chefs — from creamy bacalhau croquettes and grilled chouriço to artisan cheeses, craft beer, and freshly shucked oysters. A definitive taste of modern Lisbon's culinary scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the São Jorge Castle (Castelo de São Jorge) perched atop Lisbon's highest hill. Wander the ancient Moorish ramparts and towers with panoramic 360-degree views over the entire city and river. Follow with a self-guided exploration of the Graça neighborhood — one of Lisbon's most authentic and least touristy hilltop districts, with stunning viewpoints (miradouros) and local tascas.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private or small-group Portuguese wine tasting experience at a dedicated wine bar such as By the Wine (José Maria da Fonseca) in Chiado, sampling premium Douro reds, aged Alentejo wines, and rare Madeiras guided by a sommelier. End the evening with a nightcap at one of Lisbon's celebrated cocktail bars.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before heading to Time Out Market.
meals.lunch: Full grazing lunch at Time Out Market Lisbon — budget approximately €25–40 per person for a generous and varied spread across multiple stalls.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez) — a multi-concept restaurant space in Chiado offering refined Portuguese cuisine with a creative, contemporary twist. The Taberna section is particularly celebrated for its petiscos.

day_by_day.notes: Time Out Market is busiest from noon onward — arriving at 11:00 allows for a more comfortable and relaxed experience. The São Jorge Castle is a moderate uphill walk from Baixa; consider a tuk-tuk or taxi to the entrance. Graça viewpoint (Miradouro da Graça) at golden hour offers arguably the finest view in Lisbon.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Lisbon. Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market in the Campo de Santa Clara (open Tuesday and Saturday mornings) for antiques, vintage azulejos, and unique Portuguese souvenirs. Browse at a relaxed pace and engage with local vendors — a wonderfully authentic Lisbon experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the final afternoon revisiting a favorite neighborhood or exploring the LX Factory, a vibrant creative hub in a converted 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara, featuring independent boutiques, art studios, bookshops, and excellent cafés. A perfect place for last-minute premium gifts and keepsakes. Alternatively, enjoy a final riverside walk along the Ribeira waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Lisbon's finest tables — a celebratory conclusion to a perfect premium trip. Return to the hotel for packing and preparation for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast, or treat yourself to a special brunch at Café de São Bento or Tartine (Chiado) — both beloved for their quality and ambiance.
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the acclaimed restaurants within LX Factory, such as O Velho Eurico or the popular Sunday market food stalls (if applicable), or a light meal at a riverside café in Alcântara.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Eleven Restaurant (1 Michelin Star) — Lisbon's iconic fine dining destination with floor-to-ceiling views over Parque Eduardo VII and the city skyline. The tasting menu with wine pairing is an unforgettable finale to a luxury Lisbon journey.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics and arrange a luxury private transfer to the airport in advance. Feira da Ladra runs from approximately 09:00–18:00 on Tuesdays — arrive early for the best finds. Eleven Restaurant requires advance reservation and smart-casual to formal attire. Allow extra time on the final day for any last-minute shopping or spontaneous discoveries in this endlessly captivating city.

query: Lisbon city break, $2500 couple, food and history, 5 days, May 2027, from Boston
